title: Localizing a flat module over an algebra
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $M$ be an $A$-module that is flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and let $S$ be a multiplicative subset of $A$. Regard $S^{-1}M$ as an $R$-module through the localization map $A\to S^{-1}A$. Then $S^{-1}M$ is flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.39.18, Tag 00HT, part (6), localization argument

proof.text: Let $N_1\to N_2$ be an injective map of $R$-modules. Since $M$ is flat over $R$, the induced map $N_1\otimes_R M\to N_2\otimes_R M$ is injective by the definition of flatness. Using the canonical symmetry isomorphisms of tensor products, regard this as the corresponding injective map $M\otimes_R N_1\to M\otimes_R N_2$. These are $A$-linear maps through the $A$-factor $M$. Localizing this map at the image of $S$ remains injective because localization of modules is exact [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], applied with base ring $A$. The natural localization-tensor identification [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], together with its naturality in $N$, identifies the localized map with $S^{-1}M\otimes_R N_1\to S^{-1}M\otimes_R N_2$, whose tensor-symmetric form is $N_1\otimes_R S^{-1}M\to N_2\otimes_R S^{-1}M$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.39.18, Tag 00HT, part (6), localization argument

proof.text: The map $N_1\otimes_R S^{-1}M\to N_2\otimes_R S^{-1}M$ is injective for every injective $R$-linear map $N_1\to N_2$. By the definition of a flat module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $S^{-1}M$ is flat over $R$.
